title: Censorship of History
snippet: In a context of censorship, the expression of criticism takes the shape of historical analogies because their creators gamble on the strength of analogies to recall precedents, to suggest a diagnosis and a remedy, and to connect the like-minded in a brief, cathartic moment. When historical analogies stick to memory, they may transform into templates for conversation, criticism, and action. In a singular gesture, the creators of analogies are able to throw light on recent injustice by talking [...] Connectivity. Historical analogies reveal a temerity to circumvent the tyrant, and audiences admire such panache. For a brief moment, these analogies forge a bond between the historians and their public and emotionally connect them in their resistance. [...] by talking about remote injustice and conjuring up freedom in times past. In contexts of repression, historical analogies challenge the present situation by evoking its double or its antipode in the past. In so doing, they arouse historical awareness and briefly bring relief. If successful, they are small victories against autocratic power. They are sparks in the dark.Footnote 39

title: New Covid variant BA.3.2 detected across US, but experts urge vigilance over alarm

While some media outlets have referred to BA.3.2 as a “highly” or “heavily” mutated variant, Veldhoen said that “heavily mutated is relative; Sars-CoV-2 is nearly 30,000 base pairs long.”

Understanding DNA-RNA-Protein – A Recipe Analogy [...] genes use a process called alternative splicing, which allows a few variations on the recipe to be made from one gene; an analogy might be a recipe for bread where you swap add-ins like garlic or nuts to get a slightly varied end product. The RNA transcript, called messenger RNA (mRNA) then can be used by the cell as instructions to make the recipe. [...] Genetic-based therapies can be complex and understanding how they work can require some knowledge of basic molecular biology; mainly understanding DNA, genes, RNA, and protein. A good analogy to help explain these relationships is to think of a recipe blog or celebrity recipe book. DNA is the entire collection of recipes; genes are individual descriptions of recipes; RNA is the recipe card with just the important instructions; and protein is the completed recipe (Figure 1).
